pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.2: Reading for Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading for Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you show love to your family members?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading for Comprehension helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING FOR COMPREHENSION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading for Comprehension is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading for Comprehension”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading for Comprehension to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading for Comprehension from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading for Comprehension: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Reading for Comprehension?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you show love to your family members?
2. How does vocabulary help in language acquisition?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading for Comprehension means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate vocabulary building for language acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
